correctness.rationale: For a partial alternating-sign matrix with unique -1 at (r,c), each row/column containing it has 1 or 2 positive arms. Frobenius squared distance lower bound δ²(1+(a-1)/2+(b-1)/2) with δ=Y_rc+1>=1 follows from saturation and Cauchy-Schwarz; the displayed zero-center and half-arm point attains (a+b)/2. Complete ASMs with one -1 are row/column-permutation equivalent to the 3x3 cross D⊕I_(n-3). Direct exact KKT potential h verifies X_ij=(A_ij-h_i-h_j)_+, nonnegative doubly stochastic rows/columns, unique nearest projection and squared distance 2+2/(n+5); choose 3 rows, 3 columns and remaining permutation to count C(n,3)^2(n-3)!. Independently built rational matrices n=3..35 and verified every row/column constraint, every complementarity entry and exact distances.
residual_risks: Tests n<=35 do not establish universal case; written Cauchy-Schwarz and KKT proof does. The count assumes the unique defect forces the canonical core, checked combinatorially.
